items.label: percentage change multiplier
items.hint: One change after another: multiply the multipliers. Up 20% then down 20% is × 0.96.

widget: money
mode: change
q: 100
a: 20
b: -20

items.label: tax brackets
items.code: \text{each part of the income} \times \text{its bracket's rate}
items.hint: The marginal rate is the rate on the last dollar; the effective rate is total tax ÷ income.

items.label: multiplying integers
items.hint: Same signs give a positive, different signs a negative. On the line: $a$ jumps of $b$; a negative number of jumps goes the opposite way.
items.board:
widget: numberline
range: -12, 12
labels: 2
product: a × b
slider a: -4, 4, -3
slider b: -4, 4, -2
items.shows: −3 jumps of −2 go the opposite way: to 6

items.label: dividing integers
items.hint: The same sign rule as multiplying, because dividing undoes it: check $3 \times (-4) = -12$.

items.label: placing a negative fraction
items.hint: Split each unit into equal parts and count from zero. A negative counts left, and the part counts further from zero, not back towards it.
items.board:
widget: numberline
range: -2, 2
fractions: 4
point A: -1.25
point B: -0.75

items.label: negative fractions and decimals
items.hint: The integer sign rules hold for every fraction and decimal. Sign first, then size.

items.label: efficient order
items.hint: Multiply in any order, pairing friendly numbers; or split a number: $6 \times (-2.5) = 6 \times (-2) + 6 \times (-0.5)$.

items.label: percentages in two steps
items.hint: Each percentage is of a different amount, so they cannot be added: 20% off then 10% off is not 30% off.

items.label: terminating and recurring
items.hint: In long division a remainder of 0 means the decimal stops; a remainder that comes back means the digits repeat. A bar (or dots) marks the repeating block.

items.label: which decimals stop
items.hint: Simplify first, then break the denominator into primes. Any prime other than 2 or 5 makes it recur, because 10 = 2 × 5.

items.label: rational and irrational
items.hint: Rational numbers are fractions: their decimals stop or repeat. Irrational numbers never stop and never repeat. √16 = 4 is rational.
items.shows: A number line to zoom in on √2

items.label: placing a square root
items.hint: Find the perfect squares either side, then square decimals to get closer. A rounded value is an approximation.

items.label: index laws
items.code: a^m \times a^n = a^{m+n} \quad a^m \div a^n = a^{m-n} \quad (a^m)^n = a^{mn}
items.hint: Write the powers out as factors to see why. Only powers of the same base combine.

mode: quotient
a: 3
m: 5
n: 2

items.label: zero index
items.hint: aⁿ ÷ aⁿ = 1, and the quotient law calls it a⁰.
